hints: Equate the line and curve equations: $x^2 + kx + 6 = 3x + k$.
Rearrange into standard quadratic form $x^2 + (k - 3)x + (6 - k) = 0$.
Set the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac > 0$ for two distinct real points of intersection and solve the quadratic inequality.
walkthrough:
Equate the curve and straight line equations to find their points of intersection:
$$x^2 + kx + 6 = 3x + k \implies x^2 + (k - 3)x + (6 - k) = 0$$

Apply the condition for two distinct intersections, namely discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac > 0$:
$$(k - 3)^2 - 4(1)(6 - k) > 0$$
$$(k^2 - 6k + 9) - (24 - 4k) > 0 \implies k^2 - 2k - 15 > 0$$

Determine the outside solution regions:
$$k < -3 \quad \text{or} \quad k > 5$$
